source: DPROD Contracts dprod-contracts/examples/baseline.ttl, policy <https://example.org/offers/country-ref> (EKGF dprod, develop, 50db943)
notes: Extracted unchanged except the three anonymous rules are named rule:ref-*. odrl:conflict is absent as in DPROD, so the profile default (odrl:prohibit) applies. ex:query is declared includedIn odrl:read as in the source vocabulary; odrl:modify includedIn odrl:use comes from the shipped ODRL action hierarchy. The offer's permissions name no assignee, so any request subject matches (due2-workflows.md §5.2: no party part to fail; DPROD formal-semantics.md §7.4: subject = ⊥ applies to any agent). DPROD Σ assumed: Σ₀ with clock = request.at. Action hierarchy is the point: a query request matches the read permission too (query ⊑ read), never the reverse; and the modify prohibition does not reach read or distribute.

scenarios.name: query the reference table

expected.why: ex:query ⊑ odrl:read, so rule:ref-query matches by equality and rule:ref-read matches by hierarchy; either gives a ready candidate, and no prohibition matches (modify does not subsume query). Permit.

scenarios.dprod_expected: Permit (both permissions active: query matches query, and query ⊑ read under the intended §7.4 reading)

scenarios.name: read the reference table

expected.why: rule:ref-read matches by equality. rule:ref-query does not: read is not below query, and the hierarchy never widens a rule upward. The prohibition does not match. Permit.

scenarios.dprod_expected: Permit (only the read permission is active; under the literal §7.4 direction the query permission would also match, which the intended reading rejects)

expected.why: rule:ref-no-modify matches by equality (read and query are not below modify, so no permission matches). A surviving, applying prohibition gives Deny.
No rule matches: distribute is below none of read, query, or modify (each sits under use, a sibling). The policy does not govern this action here, which is NotApplicable, not Deny.
